database_summary: Cricket match event database (SQLite) with tables for players, teams, matches, player participation, ball-by-ball events and derived per-ball tables (batsman runs, wickets, extras). Row counts show a moderate-size event-level dataset (ball_by_ball ~134k rows). Schema includes foreign keys by naming conventions (player_id, team_id, match_id) but no explicit FK constraints in DDL. Many tables use composite natural keys (match, over, ball, innings).

accepted.name: player_dim
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  player_id,
  player_name,
  dob,
  batting_hand,
  bowling_skill,
  country_name
FROM player
accepted.description: Canonicalized player dimension: one row per player with original player attributes preserved for joins and downstream labeling. Use when you need player attributes (name, country, batting/bowling) joined to event or match-level data. | Use for: List players and their attributes; Filter players by batting_hand, bowling_skill or country_name; Join player attributes to ball-by-ball, wickets or matches

accepted.name: team_dim
accepted.description: Canonicalized team dimension: one row per team preserving team id and name for joining to matches and events. | Use for: Resolve team names for match or event reports; Aggregate team-level stats by joining to matches or ball_by_ball

accepted.name: match_dim
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  match_id,
  team_1,
  team_2,
  match_date,
  season_id,
  venue,
  toss_winner,
  toss_decision,
  win_type,
  win_margin,
  outcome_type,
  match_winner,
  man_of_the_match
FROM match
accepted.description: Canonicalized match dimension: one row per match preserving identifiers and key match attributes. Use to join match-level context (date, venue, teams, winner) to event data. | Use for: Match-level summaries; Filter matches by season_id, venue, match_date or outcome_type; Join match info to ball_by_ball or player_match

accepted.name: player_match_participation
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  pm.match_id,
  pm.player_id,
  pm.role,
  pm.team_id,
  p.player_name,
  p.dob,
  p.batting_hand,
  p.bowling_skill,
  p.country_name,
  t.name AS name
FROM player_match pm
LEFT JOIN player p ON pm.player_id = p.player_id
LEFT JOIN team t ON pm.team_id = t.team_id
accepted.description: One row per player-match participation enriched with player attributes and team name. Use to find which players participated for which team in a match and to join player metadata. | Use for: Who played for a given team in a match; Player rosters per match; Filter participants by player attributes or role

accepted.name: ball_event_base
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.match_id,
  b.innings_no,
  b.over_id,
  b.ball_id,
  b.team_batting,
  b.team_bowling,
  b.striker_batting_position,
  b.striker,
  b.non_striker,
  b.bowler,
  bs.runs_scored,
  er.extra_type,
  er.extra_runs,
  wt.player_out,
  wt.kind_out
FROM ball_by_ball b
LEFT JOIN batsman_scored bs
  ON b.match_id = bs.match_id
  AND b.innings_no = bs.innings_no
  AND b.over_id = bs.over_id
  AND b.ball_id = bs.ball_id
LEFT JOIN extra_runs er
  ON b.match_id = er.match_id
  AND b.innings_no = er.innings_no
  AND b.over_id = er.over_id
  AND b.ball_id = er.ball_id
LEFT JOIN wicket_taken wt
  ON b.match_id = wt.match_id
  AND b.innings_no = wt.innings_no
  AND b.over_id = wt.over_id
  AND b.ball_id = wt.ball_id
accepted.description: One row per ball delivery (the event grain) combining ball_by_ball with batsman runs, extras and wicket info. Preserves identifying keys for joins and exposes measures needed to compute per-delivery runs and dismissals. | Use for: Compute total runs per innings/match/team by summing runs_scored + extra_runs; Find deliveries that resulted in wickets and their kinds; Filter deliveries by bowler/striker or by extra_type

accepted.name: runs_per_delivery
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  match_id,
  innings_no,
  over_id,
  ball_id,
  striker,
  bowler,
  COALESCE(runs_scored, 0) AS runs_scored,
  COALESCE(extra_runs, 0) AS extra_runs,
  (COALESCE(runs_scored,0) + COALESCE(extra_runs,0)) AS total_runs_on_ball,
  CASE WHEN player_out IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_wicket
FROM (
  SELECT
    b.match_id,
    b.innings_no,
    b.over_id,
    b.ball_id,
    b.striker,
    b.bowler,
    bs.runs_scored,
    er.extra_runs,
    wt.player_out
  FROM ball_by_ball b
  LEFT JOIN batsman_scored bs
    ON b.match_id = bs.match_id
    AND b.innings_no = bs.innings_no
    AND b.over_id = bs.over_id
    AND b.ball_id = bs.ball_id
  LEFT JOIN extra_runs er
    ON b.match_id = er.match_id
    AND b.innings_no = er.innings_no
    AND b.over_id = er.over_id
    AND b.ball_id = er.ball_id
  LEFT JOIN wicket_taken wt
    ON b.match_id = wt.match_id
    AND b.innings_no = wt.innings_no
    AND b.over_id = wt.over_id
    AND b.ball_id = wt.ball_id
)
accepted.description: Aggregated measure at the ball delivery grain giving total runs contributed by batsman and extras and a flag for wicket. Useful for computing innings or match totals and for per-ball analytics. | Use for: Total runs by innings/match/team/bowler/batsman; Wicket counts by bowler or over; Compute strike rates or economy using runs and deliveries

accepted.name: bowler_aggregates
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  match_id,
  bowler,
  COUNT(1) AS deliveries_bowled,
  SUM(total_runs_on_ball) AS runs_conceded,
  SUM(is_wicket) AS wickets_in_match
FROM (
  SELECT
    b.match_id,
    b.innings_no,
    b.over_id,
    b.ball_id,
    b.bowler,
    COALESCE(bs.runs_scored,0) + COALESCE(er.extra_runs,0) AS total_runs_on_ball,
    CASE WHEN wt.player_out IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_wicket
  FROM ball_by_ball b
  LEFT JOIN batsman_scored bs
    ON b.match_id = bs.match_id
    AND b.innings_no = bs.innings_no
    AND b.over_id = bs.over_id
    AND b.ball_id = bs.ball_id
  LEFT JOIN extra_runs er
    ON b.match_id = er.match_id
    AND b.innings_no = er.innings_no
    AND b.over_id = er.over_id
    AND b.ball_id = er.ball_id
  LEFT JOIN wicket_taken wt
    ON b.match_id = wt.match_id
    AND b.innings_no = wt.innings_no
    AND b.over_id = wt.over_id
    AND b.ball_id = wt.ball_id
)
GROUP BY
  match_id,
  bowler
accepted.description: Bowler-level aggregated stats per match and across matches: counts of deliveries, total runs conceded and wickets taken per bowler per match. Use for match reports or career aggregates (aggregate further across match_id). | Use for: Who bowled the most deliveries or took most wickets in a match; Compute bowler economy (runs_conceded / (deliveries/6)) after further calculation; Aggregate bowler stats across matches by summing over match_id

accepted.name: batsman_aggregates
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  match_id,
  striker AS player_id,
  COUNT(1) AS balls_faced,
  SUM(COALESCE(runs_scored,0)) AS runs_scored
FROM (
  SELECT
    b.match_id,
    b.innings_no,
    b.over_id,
    b.ball_id,
    b.striker,
    bs.runs_scored
  FROM ball_by_ball b
  LEFT JOIN batsman_scored bs
    ON b.match_id = bs.match_id
    AND b.innings_no = bs.innings_no
    AND b.over_id = bs.over_id
    AND b.ball_id = bs.ball_id
)
GROUP BY
  match_id,
  striker
accepted.description: Batsman-level aggregated stats per match: total runs scored and balls faced per striker per match. Useful for innings scorecards and per-match batting metrics. | Use for: Top scorers in a match; Compute batsman strike rate (runs / balls_faced) after joining runs and balls; Career aggregates by summing across match_id

accepted.name: match_team_summary
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  be.match_id,
  be.team_batting AS team_id,
  SUM(COALESCE(be.runs_scored,0) + COALESCE(be.extra_runs,0)) AS total_runs,
  SUM(CASE WHEN be.player_out IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS total_wickets,
  MIN(be.innings_no) AS sample_innings_no -- preserved to indicate an innings number when relevant
FROM (
  SELECT
    b.match_id,
    b.innings_no,
    b.over_id,
    b.ball_id,
    b.team_batting,
    bs.runs_scored,
    er.extra_runs,
    wt.player_out
  FROM ball_by_ball b
  LEFT JOIN batsman_scored bs
    ON b.match_id = bs.match_id
    AND b.innings_no = bs.innings_no
    AND b.over_id = bs.over_id
    AND b.ball_id = bs.ball_id
  LEFT JOIN extra_runs er
    ON b.match_id = er.match_id
    AND b.innings_no = er.innings_no
    AND b.over_id = er.over_id
    AND b.ball_id = er.ball_id
  LEFT JOIN wicket_taken wt
    ON b.match_id = wt.match_id
    AND b.innings_no = wt.innings_no
    AND b.over_id = wt.over_id
    AND b.ball_id = wt.ball_id
) be
GROUP BY
  be.match_id,
  be.team_batting
accepted.description: Per-match, per-team summary (both sides): aggregates of runs and wickets for each batting team in a match. Use to produce innings/team scorecards and match-level comparisons. | Use for: Innings totals per team in a match; Compare team scores in a match; Identify innings by team and join to match table for winner determination

accepted.name: bowler_career_rank_by_wickets
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  bowler,
  SUM(is_wicket) AS total_wickets,
  RANK() OVER (ORDER BY SUM(is_wicket) DESC) AS wickets_rank
FROM (
  SELECT
    b.bowler,
    CASE WHEN wt.player_out IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_wicket
  FROM ball_by_ball b
  LEFT JOIN wicket_taken wt
    ON b.match_id = wt.match_id
    AND b.innings_no = wt.innings_no
    AND b.over_id = wt.over_id
    AND b.ball_id = wt.ball_id
)
GROUP BY
  bowler
accepted.description: Bowler ranking across all matches by total wickets (global rank). Use as a building block to get top bowlers overall; downstream queries can filter on wickets_rank. | Use for: Top wicket takers overall; Filter top bowlers by wickets_rank; Leaderboards for bowlers
